findingDetails.title: Registry paths are not resolved relative to the registry's own package root
findingDetails.evidence: The registry stores runtime/cli-prefixed paths from inside runtime/cli and lists dist outputs absent in the current source-only checkout; no consumer contract declares the intended resolution root.
findingDetails.recommendation: Define the registry resolution root and distinguish source paths from build outputs, then replay the registry consumer if one is introduced.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Direct registry read, filesystem existence checks for listed script paths and repository search for registry consumers.

findingDetails.title: Current subordinate READMEs retain retired scripts topology
findingDetails.evidence: Continuity documentation describes dependencies as scripts/core, scripts/extractors, scripts/loaders, scripts/renderers and scripts/lib even though those directories are now under runtime/cli.
findingDetails.recommendation: Rewrite current subordinate dependency diagrams to use runtime/cli paths while preserving external skill script references.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Direct reads across continuity, retrieval, rules and core READMEs found the same stale vocabulary.

findingDetails.title: Public runtime API comments retain old consumer names
findingDetails.evidence: Comments refer to scripts/spec-folder, scripts/graph and scripts/core while current callers are in runtime/cli.
findingDetails.recommendation: Refresh public API boundary comments on the next scoped documentation pass.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Direct read of API comments and current runtime/cli package layout.
